content:
mira (Sales): Hi team — Greencrest sent an RFI (attached) and a short security questionnaire. They want a capability matrix + POC timeline by EOD Friday. Can we coordinate?

sam (Solutions): I can drive the capability matrix. quick q: do they need dedicated capacity in the POC or is hosted ok?

mira (Sales): They mentioned 'reserved capacity' in the RFI but said they might accept hosted for the initial POC to speed things up.

jordan (SE): For the POC we can use hosted with a pinned model version. It matches most of their asks and keeps infra overhead low. If they need throughput guarantees we can offer a short dedicated window.

cameron (AE): Pricing question from procurement: "what's the delta between pay-as-you-go and a 3-month reserved commit for 8 GPUs?" Any quick numbers?

sam (Solutions): Rough calc: PAYG baseline ~ $X.XX/token equivalent. 3-month reserved (8x A100-class) ~ 40% lower unit cost assuming 60% utilization. I'll put exacts in the matrix.

aoife (Security): I skimmed the questionnaire. Two blockers: 1) they ask for SOC2 cert date and 2) egress controls for private deployments. I can draft answers but need confirmation on KMS integration options for Private.

mira (Sales): @aoife — they can accept KMS but prefer HSM. Do we have an HSM option for Private?

aoife (Security): We support customer KMS and HSM-backed keys on Private; note: HSM requires a bit more provisioning lead time. I'll add recommended language.

sam (Solutions): Uploading an initial matrix now: https://redwood.docs/internal/greencrest-capability-matrix-v1 (placeholder) 

[sam (Solutions) attached file: Redwood-capability-matrix-v3.xlsx]

jordan (SE): Quick technical note for the matrix: add a row for "graceful degradation" — fallback to smaller quantized model + region routing. Greencrest asked about regulatory failover.

mira (Sales): Good call. Also include rollout options (canary/A-B) and eval hooks.

cameron (AE): I'll handle procurement outreach. Greencrest-procurement: can you confirm if they require SOC2 Type II or if SOC2 Type I is acceptable for the POC?

greencrest-procurement: SOC2 Type II required for production, Type I is fine for a limited POC. Thanks.

aoife (Security): I'll draft the security Q answers and flag any items that need legal signoff. Expect a draft in ~3 hours.

sam (Solutions): For the POC timeline proposed:
```
- Day 0: Kickoff + scoping
- Day 3: Hosted endpoint + sample dataset ingest
- Day 7: Integration + metrics dashboard
- Day 14: Load/latency validation + handoff
```
This assumes hosted; add 2–3 weeks if we provision dedicated GPUs/HSM.

mira (Sales): Perfect. Can someone turn the timeline + matrix + security Q into a single zip for them? I can send.

sam (Solutions): I'll export matrix + short technical appendix.

aoife (Security): I'll attach the questionnaire answers and HSM note.

cameron (AE): I'll draft a short commercial note (pricing options) and signposting to Enterprise SLA.

mira (Sales): Great — action items: @sam produce final matrix, @aoife security answers, @cameron pricing note. I’ll assemble and send by Friday EOD. :thumbsup:

jordan (SE): ping me if they want a deeper perf run, I can schedule bench windows.

mira (Sales): Thanks all — sending provisional reply now to buy time with a summary and expected deliverable ETA.

[sent message to Greencrest: "Thanks — we'll deliver capability matrix, POC timeline, and security questionnaire responses by Friday EOD. Rep: mira@redwood.com"]
